fig_matched_camp_models: \textbf{Numerical disagreement persists with a single Gaussian.} (a) Distance $\|\langle\mu\rangle_{\mathrm{gas}}-\langle\mu\rangle_{\mathrm{mass}}\|_2$ in the common observable coordinates $(C,G,M)$. The horizontal axis in (a) is logarithmic; the distance axis includes zero. The two Gaussian arms share one information-pooled reference; the gated arm reweights the same social matrix using entering-mean disagreement ($\nu=.01$). Candidate predictions use the posterior mixture mean. Model weights are private in green and shared with $\alpha_m=.02$ in blue; conditional sharing is enabled throughout. (b) Gas (solid) and mass (dotted) group-mean oxygen probabilities for the two candidate arms; the single Gaussian has no corresponding theory probability. (c) Full-signal predictive MSE averaged over states 3,751--5,000: gas circles and open mass squares. Plain and Gate denote Gaussian and gated Gaussian; Priv. and Share denote private and shared candidate weights. Var. is the candidate/private arm with only the release gas residual variance changed from .5 to .5448. Distinct single-Gaussian predictions under sustained selective observations are not evidence of distinct theoretical commitments. Means and pointwise 95\% percentile intervals use 2,000 whole-seed bootstrap resamples of all 50 paired seeds (10,000--10,049). The candidate trajectories reuse the previous runs with exactly the same observation streams: this is a paired extension, not an independent replication. Every displayed update is retained without smoothing. All arms have 16 agents, fixed gas/mass observation groups, $\beta=.05$, $\omega=.3$, $\sigma_o=.5$, and the constant full signal $(C,G,M)=(1,1,1)$.
fig_matched_camp_diagnostics: \textbf{Reference compression and readout choices affect the comparison.} (a) Gaussian (orange) and gated Gaussian (red) distances: information-pool (solid) or equal-mixture moment-matched (dashed) references, including between-candidate mean covariance. Panels (a,b) use logarithmic time. (b) Realized cross-group weight before each observation: information-pool reference (purple), moment reference (grey); gas (solid), mass (dotted). Dashed horizontal: ungated weight .05. (c) Candidate/private (green) and candidate/shared (blue) distances using mixture means (solid) and selected-candidate/MAP means (dashed). (d) Three different quantities over states 3,751--5,000: the mean instantaneous norm (grey circle), the seed-average norm after time-averaging the signed camp difference (blue square), and the norm after both time and seed averaging (open orange triangle). Plain, Gate, Priv. and Share denote Gaussian, gated Gaussian, candidates/private and candidates/shared, respectively. The last two distance definitions distinguish time-averaged directional differences from fluctuations. The orange triangle is a descriptive point without an interval: a norm alone cannot establish a nonzero ensemble mean. All hidden candidate-specific coordinates are excluded. Means and pointwise 95\% percentile intervals use 2,000 whole-seed bootstrap resamples of all 50 paired seeds (10,000--10,049). The candidate trajectories reuse the previous runs with exactly the same observation streams: this is a paired extension, not an independent replication. Every displayed update is retained without smoothing. All arms have 16 agents, fixed gas/mass observation groups, $\beta=.05$, $\omega=.3$, $\sigma_o=.5$, and the constant full signal $(C,G,M)=(1,1,1)$.
